name: Sandy Inundation Zone
description:
This dataset contains polygon records delineating areas inundated by Hurricane Sandy storm surge, clipped to a 1,000-foot buffer around the HSIP (Homeland Security Infrastructure Program) boundary. Each of the 492 sampled rows represents a mapped inundation zone in New York, with metadata describing how the zone was produced. The fields include the state, the elevation data source (New York City OEM 1-meter), the mapping status (Final Field-Verified High Resolution), the source data (USGS Mission Assignment, high-water marks, and surge sensors), a verification flag (Yes), and a descriptive comment. An ID column is present but holds a constant value of zero across all rows.

Because the attributes are uniform in this sample, the dataset functions primarily as a spatial layer of Sandy surge extent rather than a multi-variable table. It could be used for coastal flood risk assessment, floodplain and insurance analysis, emergency planning and recovery studies, infrastructure exposure screening, and research on storm surge impacts in
